manifest_scope: one entry per current Git-tracked path, including files handled without an embedded header

dates.created: earliest traceable Git content-introduction date, following rename history; otherwise unknown with reason
dates.updated: latest traceable content-change date after excluding the metadata block; otherwise unknown with reason
dates.git_timestamp_field: committer date, converted to UTC calendar date

revision.increment_when: content outside the metadata block changes
revision.do_not_increment_when: only metadata fields or the metadata block change

manifest_record_requirements.purpose: file-specific responsibility, important input/output, and applicable boundary
manifest_record_requirements.third_party_attribution: preserve upstream author, copyright and license notices verbatim; add Bai Junhao only as project maintainer
manifest_record_requirements.rights_reference: See LICENSE; do not infer SPDX or OSI approval

file_classes.reason: Preserve the operative license language and its own copyright notice; keep repository metadata out of the legal text.

file_classes.syntax: Go line comments before package; after build constraints and required blank line
file_classes.notes: Preserve //go:build, // +build, generated-code markers, and existing copyright comments.

file_classes.syntax: Python # comments after shebang and encoding cookie
JavaScript/TypeScript line comments before imports and after directives
Native # comments only when accepted before content by the actual consumer
file_classes.notes: If a tool or parser rejects a leading comment, use manifest-only and record the exact path-specific reason.

file_classes.syntax: Native # comments; keep metadata block after required format/version declarations if any

file_classes.reason: JSON has no comment syntax; preserve strict JSON and public/schema contract bytes.
Tool-owned module and lock formats must remain in their native form; do not insert metadata comments or fields.
Historical migration bytes are subject to application and integrity checks; metadata must not alter them.
Fixture bytes are regression inputs or expected outputs; record each exact path and its test purpose in the manifest.
Do not modify payload or embedded metadata; record each asset's source, purpose, and rights evidence.
The generated file is verified against its generator output; a manual header would be overwritten or cause drift.
The file contains a Unicode Consortium source URL and verbatim copyright/disclaimer. Preserve the entire existing notice and record upstream authorship separately from project maintenance.

unclassified_file_policy: Do not infer a comment syntax or purpose. Add a reviewed class or path rule before the complete inventory is accepted.

future_issues.124: Apply eligible metadata headers and refresh the canonical manifest after reconciling new tracked paths.
future_issues.125: Implement validation of exact tracked-file coverage, schema, header mirror, exceptions, dates, and revision transitions.

rule_precedence: Exact path rules override generated/third-party/frozen file classes, which override extension classes; each manifest record must match the narrowest applicable rule.
manifest_follow_up: Issue #124 applies eligible headers and refreshes this same canonical manifest for newly tracked paths; it does not create a competing inventory.
